nodes.description: Missense variants and in-frame deletions/duplications clustering in the histidine-rich region (HRR) of the Atrophin-1 domain. Protein modeling in the 2026 cohort found these to be structurally stabilizing, which is why a gain-of-function or dominant-negative mechanism is proposed rather than loss of dosage. This class is associated with more multisystem phenotypes and usually arises de novo. Which of gain-of-function or dominant-negative applies is not resolved; that either/or is kept open in the discussions block rather than being decided here.

nodes.description: RERE normally restrains sonic hedgehog (shh) and fgf8 signaling during patterning. NEDBEH-associated human RERE variants behave as hypomorphs in their ability to repress shh signaling, and some show abnormal nuclear localization. In the zebrafish rerea mutant this manifests as expanded fgf8 and pax2a expression domains in the optic stalk with reduced vax1, and in a patient-derived CRISPR knock-in cell line as downregulated SHH signaling with reciprocal upregulation of the Hippo pathway. The direction of the shh change differs between these systems, which is recorded as an open question rather than resolved here.

nodes.description: Two separable ocular mechanisms operate. First, a patterning defect: the zebrafish rerea (babyface) mutant recapitulates the optic fissure closure defect seen in humans, arising from expansion of the proximal retinal optic stalk and reduced expression of ventral retinal fate genes; inhibiting shh signaling with HPI-1 rescues the coloboma, establishing deregulated shh as causal in that model. Second, a cell-survival defect: RERE is expressed in a subset of retinal ganglion cells, the lens epithelium, and the ciliary body, and RERE-deficient mice show apoptosis of retinal cells in the ganglion cell layer from E17.5, reduced retinal ganglion cell numbers, and consequent retinal and optic nerve atrophy. Together these account for the coloboma, microphthalmia, and optic nerve findings of NEDBEH.

nodes.description: Structural CNS anomalies are recurrent in NEDBEH and include hypoplasia or thinning of the corpus callosum, reduced white matter volume, ventriculomegaly, and a small or abnormal cerebellar vermis. RERE-deficient mice show brain hypoplasia with decreased numbers of NeuN-positive hippocampal neurons, giving a cellular correlate for reduced brain growth. Retinoic acid signaling is required for hindbrain segmentation and morphogenesis, which is the proposed route to the posterior fossa findings, including the Chiari type I malformation reported in one adult. The mechanistic account of the posterior-fossa phenotypes is inferential rather than directly demonstrated.

nodes.description: Atrioventricular septation depends on endocardial cells in the AV canal undergoing epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and migrating into the cardiac jelly to populate the endocardial cushions. RERE-deficient mouse embryos have fewer mesenchymal cells in their AV endocardial cushions because both EMT and mesenchymal proliferation are reduced. In the endocardium RERE colocalizes with GATA4, positively regulates transcription from the Gata4 promoter, and Gata4 levels fall in the AV canal of RERE-deficient embryos; Rere and Gata4 interact genetically in the development of congenital heart defects. Notably, endocardium-specific Rere ablation produces hypocellular cushions, defective EMT, and ventricular septal defects WITHOUT reducing GATA4, so the cell-autonomous endocardial role of RERE must be mediated by targets other than GATA4 — the entry keeps both arms rather than collapsing them.

nodes.description: RERE is a positive regulator of retinoic acid (RA) signaling. It forms a complex with NR2F2, p300, and a retinoic acid receptor that is recruited to the retinoic acid response elements of RA target genes such as the Rarb promoter, and knockdown of NR2F2 and/or RERE decreases RA signaling. RERE is also the co-repressor-recruiting subunit of the WHHERE complex (Wdr5, Hdac1, Hdac2, Rere), which together with the RERE-binding histone methyltransferase Ehmt2/G9a becomes enriched at RA target genes upon RA treatment to promote RNA polymerase II recruitment. Loss of this activity blunts the RA-dependent transcriptional programs that pattern the embryo. Because RA acts as a morphogen across hindbrain, eye, heart, otic, and renal development, a single lesion here propagates into anomalies of several organs at once.

nodes.description: The convergent consequence: a single lesion in a retinoic-acid co-regulator expressed across the developing embryo produces coordinated anomalies of brain, eye, heart, inner ear, kidney and genitourinary tract rather than an isolated organ defect. The mouse allelic series makes this concrete — one graded reduction in Rere dosage yields microphthalmia, growth deficiency, brain hypoplasia, hearing loss, cardiovascular malformations, and renal agenesis together. The allelic class determines how much of this field is affected in a given individual: loss-of-function alleles produce fewer multisystem anomalies, whereas HRR missense variants and in-frame HRR duplications produce more.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a heterozygous pathogenic variant in RERE at 1p36.23. RERE encodes a large, widely expressed atrophin-family nuclear receptor co-regulator (atrophin-2) that scaffolds transcriptional complexes through its ELM2, SANT, and Atrophin-1 domains. Two mechanistically distinct allelic classes converge on this node. Nonsense, frameshift, canonical splice-site, and whole- or partial-gene deletion alleles reduce RERE dosage by haploinsufficiency, with nonsense-mediated decay demonstrated for at least one frameshift allele. Missense and in-frame variants clustering in a histidine-rich region (HRR) of the Atrophin-1 domain are instead structurally stabilizing, which is why they are proposed to act by a gain-of-function or dominant-negative mechanism rather than by simple loss of dosage — and why they carry a heavier multisystem burden.

nodes.description: RERE is broadly expressed in the palate during mouse embryonic development, and most RERE-deficient mouse embryos on a C57BL/6 background have cleft palate. Ablating Rere specifically in cranial neural crest cells with a Wnt1-Cre driver delays elevation of the palatal shelves and produces cleft palate, with significantly reduced proliferation of palatal shelf mesenchymal cells. This is the orofacial clefting arm of the disorder; cleft palate and cleft lip are each documented in single individuals with NEDBEH, so this node explains a rare rather than a core feature.

nodes.description: Rere-null mice die of cardiac failure between E9.5 and E11.5, which prevents study of later development. To get past that lethality the authors built an allelic series combining the null om allele with a novel ENU-derived hypomorphic allele, eyes3. The resulting graded-dosage animals reproduce the multi-organ pattern of human NEDBEH in a single genotype series: microphthalmia, postnatal growth deficiency, brain hypoplasia with reduced NeuN-positive hippocampal neurons, hearing loss, cardiovascular malformations including perimembranous ventricular septal defects, spontaneous cardiac fibrosis, and renal agenesis. This is the model ClinGen cites as recapitulating the human phenotype.

nodes.description: The zebrafish rerea mutant recapitulates the optic fissure closure defect of human NEDBEH, with an enlarged optic stalk, coloboma, and disruption of the optic stalk/neuroretina boundary. Mechanistically the defect tracks with deregulated shh signaling: expanded fgf8 and pax2a domains, reduced vax1 in the optic stalk, and — the decisive experiment — pharmacological rescue of the coloboma by the shh inhibitor HPI-1. The same study tested NEDBEH-associated human RERE variants and found them hypomorphic for shh repression, which is what connects the fish phenotype to the human alleles.
